name: Bar-Jesus
overview: Bar-Jesus was a male Jewish false prophet known from the book of Acts. His identity is marked by his role in opposing the apostles' message during their missionary journey. No additional tribal or familial background is provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Bar-Jesus means 'son of Jesus,' highlighting his Jewish heritage. He is also called Elymas, though the meaning of this name is not given. Both names are proper names referenced in Acts 13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Bar-Jesus beyond what is indicated in his name and unique attribute as a Jewish false prophet.
scriptureSignificance: Bar-Jesus is significant in the biblical narrative as an opponent to the gospel, embodying false prophecy among the Jewish people. His confrontation with the apostles illustrates the spiritual opposition faced by early Christian missionaries. His presence in Acts highlights the challenge of discerning true from false teaching in the spread of the gospel.
